title: Date-based photo renamer, dry-run, safe to run twice
prompt: I have a folder of phone photos named like IMG_20230415_120301.jpg or scan 2021_12_31.jpg. Write rename_photos.py (standard library only), run as `python3 rename_photos.py FOLDER [--dry-run]`, that renames each photo to the date in its name, YYYY-MM-DD plus the extension in lower case. When several photos share a date, the later ones in name order get -2, -3 and so on, and nothing is ever overwritten; a file already named that way is left alone. Files with no valid date, and sub-folders, stay untouched. --dry-run prints what it would do and changes nothing. It runs from cron, so a second run must be harmless. photos/ has a few samples to try it on.

files.content:
"""Grader: run rename_photos.py on a fixture folder, dry then real then again."""
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = Path("rename_photos.py").resolve()
FILES = [
    "IMG_20230415_120301.jpg", "IMG_20230415_180000.JPG", "2023-04-15.jpg",
    "holiday-2022-07-04-beach.png", "scan 2021_12_31.jpg", "VID_20200229_1.mp4",
    "IMG_20231345.jpg", "notes.txt", "IMG_20190101_a.jpeg", "IMG_20190101_b.jpeg",
]
WANT = sorted([
    "2023-04-15.jpg", "2023-04-15-2.jpg", "2023-04-15-3.jpg", "2022-07-04.png",
    "2021-12-31.jpg", "2020-02-29.mp4", "IMG_20231345.jpg", "notes.txt",
    "2019-01-01.jpeg", "2019-01-01-2.jpeg",
])


def snap(root):
    return sorted((str(p.relative_to(root)), p.read_bytes() if p.is_file() else b"<dir>")
                  for p in root.rglob("*"))


def run(*args):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"exit {r.returncode} for {args}: {r.stderr.strip()[-100:]}")
    return r


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp) / "pics"
    (root / "sub").mkdir(parents=True)
    for name in FILES:
        (root / name).write_text("content of " + name)
    (root / "sub" / "IMG_20230101.jpg").write_text("nested")
    before = snap(root)
    run(str(root), "--dry-run")
    if snap(root) != before:
        sys.exit("--dry-run changed the folder")
    run(str(root))
    got = sorted(p.name for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_file())
    if got != WANT:
        sys.exit(f"wrong names: {sorted(set(got) ^ set(WANT))}")
    if (root / "2023-04-15.jpg").read_text() != "content of 2023-04-15.jpg":
        sys.exit("an existing dated file was overwritten")
    if (root / "2023-04-15-2.jpg").read_text() != "content of IMG_20230415_120301.jpg":
        sys.exit("collision order is not by original name")
    if (root / "sub" / "IMG_20230101.jpg").read_text() != "nested" or len(list(root.glob("sub/*"))) != 1:
        sys.exit("sub-folder was touched")
    once = snap(root)
    run(str(root))
    if snap(root) != once:
        sys.exit("second run changed the folder")
    run(str(root), "--dry-run")
    if snap(root) != once:
        sys.exit("dry-run after rename changed the folder")
print("renamer ok")

notes: Grader builds its own fixture (collisions with an existing dated file, upper-case extension, leap day, invalid date, nested folder), runs dry-run, real run, a second run and checks every outcome. Null is the untouched setup: no script.
